small_guidance:
- Add autotune configs with larger BLOCK_OW (256, 512) and smaller BLOCK_OC (32) since IC=64 is small and the GEMM-K dim is tiny (IC=64); the inner dot is 64x64 which is bandwidth-bound — larger spatial tiles amortize weight loads.
- Pre-pack weights so the kh/kw inner loop is contiguous: lay out as [OC, KH_par_groups, KW_par_groups, IC] per parity so the per-(kh,kw) weight load is a single contiguous [IC, BLOCK_OC] tile with no strided gather.
- Try num_stages=4 with BLOCK_OW=128/BLOCK_OC=64 to better overlap the x gather (which is the latency-bound op) with the dot.
large_guidance:
- Switch from per-output gather to a true im2col-style GEMM where output is tiled as (N*OH*OW_tile, OC) and K = IC * (KH/STRIDE) * (KW/STRIDE) per parity; with KH=KW=4, stride=2, parity reduces K to IC*4=256, giving a clean 128x64x256 GEMM that maps well to tensor cores.
- Use channels-last (NHWC) input layout so the IC axis is the contiguous K dimension — current NCHW forces strided loads of x across IC for every (ih,iw). A one-time NHWC transpose of x amortizes over the heavy conv.
- Consider a persistent-CTA scheme: launch one CTA per SM, iterate over (n, oh, ow_tile, oc_tile) tiles internally to reduce launch overhead and reuse weight tiles across multiple output rows (oh, oh+1 share many input rows when stride=2).
